sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Pickaway County?
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the Pickaway County Recorder's Office, 110 Island Road, Suite G, Circleville, Ohio 43113, in the Pickaway County Service Center. The phone number is (740) 474-5826.

The office holds land records back to the county's start in 1810. The recorder's own words describe the job as making a clear record of deeds, mortgages, easements, plats, land surveys, powers of attorney, leases and the liens that can attach to real estate. Staff do not prepare documents and cannot say whether a title is clear.

Plan your timing. Since April 1, 2025, documents brought in after 3:30 p.m. are not recorded until the first thing on the next business day. Staff still review them and check the fees at the counter.

sections.h2: Can you mail or e-record a deed in Pickaway County?
sections.html:
Mailing works only for originals that do not need approval stamps. The recorder's page explains that the Engineer Map Department and the Auditor will not accept documents through the mail, and the recorder cannot route them. A deed that needs those stamps must be carried in, and so must a transfer on death designation.

E-recording has been offered since 2017 through a third-party vendor chosen by the submitter. Files can be sent any day, and staff process them from 8:00 a.m. to 3:45 p.m. on business days. Documents with a new survey or new legal description cannot be e-recorded and must be walked through in person.

  • Bring or mail the original with a self-addressed, stamped envelope.
  • Pay by cash, check, or card, and expect a card charge of $1.00 or 3%, whichever is greater.
  • If a deed was signed electronically and printed, a separate authenticator certificate must be attached.

sections.h2: What are the recording and copy fees in Pickaway County?
sections.html:
The base price follows the state schedule in Revised Code 317.32: $34 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after that, split between a base fee and a housing trust fund fee. Pickaway County adds the optional preservation surcharge. The recorder's page says that from January 1, 2025, basic recording fees include a $5.00 per document surcharge, which goes into the county general fund for preservation and digitization of records.

sections.h2: What does the Pickaway County auditor require before a deed is transferred?
sections.html:
The auditor's site states the conveyance fee as $3.00 per thousand, for real estate and manufactured homes. Under state law the seller pays it, and the auditor will not transfer an instrument without a completed DTE 100 or DTE 100EX form.

The county's Transfer and Conveyance Standards, adopted by the auditor and engineer under section 319.203, add more requirements:

  • The deed carries the original signature of the grantor and cannot be a fax or a copy.
  • It shows the auditor's parcel number, the site address, the prior deed reference and the grantee's tax mailing address.
  • A grantor who is not the prior grantee needs an explanation in the deed or an affidavit.
  • A new legal description needs the Engineer's Tax Map Department to stamp it "Mathematically Approved" first.
  • A split leaving a parcel of 20 acres or less needs planning commission approval.
  • A trust conveying property files an affidavit under section 5302.171 before or with the deed.

sections.h2: How do you search Pickaway County records online?
sections.html:
The recorder uses a site called CountyFusion. Indexes run from 1/1/1990 to the present by name, historical indexes cover 1810 to 1990, and most images go back to 1980. Official Records began on April 16, 1996, and earlier records sit in separate books for deeds, mortgages, leases and other types.

You need a name to search. If you only have an address, look up the owner on the auditor's website first. Images found online can be downloaded and printed for free, while older documents can be ordered by volume and page for $2.00 a page.

The office also offers a free alert, called FRAUDSLEUTH, that warns you when a document is recorded under names you enter. A sheriff's sale list is on the sheriff's website instead of the recorder's.

sections.h2: Does a paid-off mortgage show up at the Pickaway County recorder?
sections.html:
Yes, as a recorded release. The recorder explains that the lender sends a Release of Mortgage, which is linked to the original mortgage in the records, and you can get a copy free on the recording site or from the office.

Unlike a car title, the deed is not held by the bank or by the recorder while you owe on the loan. You should have received the original after closing, and the office can copy a recorded deed if yours is lost.

To change the tax mailing address, call the Pickaway County Treasurer at (740) 474-2370. Changing the name on a deed requires a new deed prepared by an attorney.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Pickaway County?
sections.html:
Pickaway County has the most residents and the highest home values of the three counties in the Census comparison used for this set of pages. The 2025 population estimate is 62,978, up 7.6% from the April 2020 estimates base, with 23,832 housing units.

  • Owner-occupied rate: 74.0%.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $256,800.
  • Median gross rent: $1,020.
  • Median household income: $74,040.
  • Building permits in 2025: 406.
  • Employer establishments in 2023: 856, with employment up 23.0% from 2022.

Compare the 406 permits with 28 in Paulding County and 39 in Perry County. Pickaway is where new construction is happening, and the county sits in the Columbus metropolitan area.

sections.h2: What is the Pickaway County landscape like for a house seller?
sections.html:
The county seat and only city is Circleville. Villages include Ashville, Commercial Point, Darbyville, Lockbourne, Harrisburg, New Holland, South Bloomfield, Tarlton and Williamsport. The Scioto River runs south through the middle of the county, Big Darby Creek drains the upper west side, and about 87% of the land is used for agriculture, according to Wikipedia.

Many sales here involve acreage, so the land-split and survey rules matter. The recorder's FAQ points to the Engineer's mapping department or GIS for property maps that are not in a recorded subdivision.

One note on the recorder's page: it carried an alert about a one-time cancellation window for Homeowner Benefit Agreements with MV Realty of Ohio that ended on April 29, 2026. If you ever signed such an agreement, ask the recorder what is recorded against your parcel before you list.

faqs.q: What time must I bring a document to the Pickaway County recorder?
faqs.a: Before 3:30 p.m. if you want it recorded that day. Documents brought in later are reviewed but not processed until the first thing the next business day.

faqs.q: Can a transfer on death designation be mailed to the Pickaway County recorder?
faqs.a: No. The recorder's page says documents that need the Engineer Map Department and Auditor stamps cannot be mailed, and it names transfer on death designations in that group.

faqs.q: How much is the conveyance fee in Pickaway County?
faqs.a: The county auditor states it as $3.00 per thousand, for both real estate and manufactured homes.

faqs.q: How do I get a copy of my recorded deed?
faqs.a: Download it free from the recorder's online site if it was recorded since the digital image coverage began, or request a copy by phone, email, mail or in person at $2.00 a page.

faqs.q: Does the recorder search my title for liens?
faqs.a: No. The office will show you how to search its records, but it cannot tell you whether title is clear. Consider a title examiner or title company for a full exam.
